architecture.mechanism: NiCr/NiSi thin-film thermocouples on polyimide substrates provide high-precision, fast-response internal temperature measurements that capture transient thermal events inside lithium-ion battery systems.
architecture.intervention: Embed NiCr/NiSi thin-film thermocouples (magnetron-sputtered on polyimide) onto Nissan Leaf battery modules/cells and wire them into the BMS so internal cell temperature is continuously monitored during Level 3 DC fast charging and operation, with an abort/threshold trip that halts charging current when internal temperature rises abnormally.
architecture.expected_effect: Early detection of localized internal heating and thermal excursions before exothermic runaway propagates, enabling the BMS to cut current and keep the battery system thermally stable, reducing the risk of thermal runaway fire.
architecture.falsification_test: Instrument a Nissan Leaf pack (and single cells) with these thin-film thermocouples, run external short-circuit, overcharge, and puncture/nail tests, and verify the sensor detects the internal temperature rise with sufficient lead time (e.g., seconds-to-minutes margin) and repeatability error near 0.45% to trigger BMS shutdown before runaway; if detection lags runaway onset or readings drift beyond spec, the mechanism is falsified.
